note: Nubank's contracts and charges page: revolving credit on the Nubank card costs between 2.75% and 19.99% a month, written at the top of the range; its card page sells it without an annual fee. Wave 3 (2026-10-30): the main banks are Itaú Unibanco, Caixa Econômica Federal and Nubank (kept from before), chosen from the largest card issuers whose terms could be read: Banco do Brasil's tariff table (bb.com.br/docs/pub/trf/tarifasPF.pdf) answered with a block page (403), and Itaú's own cards page and Santander's refused (403), Bradesco's sits behind Akamai. Itaú's general table of card tariffs for individuals (in force from 1 October 2026), read in full: each of its 215 personal cards, own-brand and partner, with its annual fee (yearly or monthly, by plan, as the table gives it; free where it says grátis) and the 18-real fee for each cash withdrawal in Brazil; the emergency credit assessment (the over-limit fee) is exempt for every card. Rows whose card name the PDF's text breaks apart (several Personnalité and Uniclass plans) and the additional-card rows aren't written. Caixa's table of priority services for individuals (published 1 October 2026): of its basic credit cards only CAIXA Sim and CAIXA Tem are still sold (the others are marked commercialization unavailable), both without an annual fee; a cash withdrawal in Brazil costs 11 reais and the emergency credit assessment, charged for going over the limit, 19 reais. Neither bank's table states a card's interest rate, so the rate written for Itaú's and Caixa's cards is the Central Bank's published average monthly rate each charged on revolving card credit (rotativo total) for the week of 9 to 16 October 2026: Itaú Unibanco 14.36%, Caixa 12.21%. The tables state no minimum payment, grace period, late fee or foreign transaction fee; the IOF tax on credit isn't stated by either bank and isn't written.
